items.title: Async Rust, Two Years In: What the Borrow Checker Actually Costs You
items.brief: The async Rust ecosystem has settled on patterns that make cancellation safety tractable, and most complaints trace back to three specific footguns. A 14-minute read held for a full sitting.

items.title: The Economics of Self-Hosting in 2026
items.brief: A worked comparison of VPS pricing, electricity, and admin hours for a small self-hosted stack against equivalent managed services. The break-even point sits around six low-traffic services, after which owning the box wins on cost and control.

items.title: A Filesystem in 1,000 Lines of Rust
items.brief: Log-structured layout, crash consistency, and exactly where the author cut corners — a worked filesystem built in a thousand lines of Rust.

items.title: RustCGo: Calling Go From Rust Without the FFI Pain
items.brief: Calling Go from Rust via cgo costs roughly 200ns per crossing and drags a second garbage collector into the process. Benchmarks show it only pays off when one specific Go library is needed; otherwise pure Rust wins.

items.title: Scheduler Tickless Designs Compared
items.brief: A fully tickless scheduler saves about 4% idle power across three hobby kernels but complicates timer handling. The hybrid design — tickless at idle, ticked under load — wins on both power and latency, and is what Linux already does.

items.title: What Teams Actually Measure When They Measure Agent Productivity
items.brief: A four-metric frame for judging how much software agents actually deliver, drawn from teams that instrument their rollouts. Worth a long sitting.

items.title: Disaster-Recovery Tabletop Templates for Small Platform Teams
items.brief: A template library for DR tabletop exercises where only one piece earns its keep: a third-party-outage scenario with pre-written injects and a 30-minute timebox. The other four templates are filler.

items.title: This Week in React #512
items.brief: The notable item in this newsletter issue is React's RSC caching RFC, which proposes default-caching fetches in both dev and prod with explicit invalidation. The community is split on whether defaults should ever cache.

items.title: The Lost Art of the Memorandum: How Writers Kept Thinking Before Notebooks
items.brief: Before personal notes were files, writers kept loose memorandums — one idea per slip, physically reshuffled while composing. The author argues the slip, not the notebook, was the real thinking tool.
